scenario: A premium retail dashboard for saree stores logs daily sales only when a store makes more than Rs 2 lakh, because smaller stores stay on an offline billing stack. The retail head wants the average daily sales across all stores.

data.description: Only daily sales above Rs 2 lakh are observed. Daily sales are modeled as Normal with known standard deviation sigma = Rs 80,000.

question: Using the truncated normal model, estimate (a) the true mean daily sales mu across all stores, and (b) the fraction of stores that appear in the premium dashboard.
naive_answer: Average daily sales are about Rs 2.388 lakh because that is the premium-dashboard mean.
naive_trap: The dashboard only includes upper-tail stores. The full-store mean is much lower than the selected-store mean.
reasoning_trace: Step 1: Solve 238800 = mu + 80000*lambda((200000-mu)/80000). Step 2: The solution has alpha about 1.2, so mu = 200000 - 1.2*80000 = 104000. Step 3: The recorded fraction is sf(1.2) = 0.1151.
python_verification:
from scipy.optimize import brentq
from scipy.stats import norm
def eq(mu):
    a=(200000-mu)/80000
    return mu + 80000*norm.pdf(a)/norm.sf(a) - 238800
mu=brentq(eq,-500000,199999)
frac=norm.sf((200000-mu)/80000)
assert abs(mu-104000) < 3000 and abs(frac-0.1151) < 0.005
